findings.reason: Verified in nodestore/base.py that get_multi dedupes, returns uncached hits before cached ones via items.update, and omits missing IDs, so zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs error IDs with the wrong events whenever cache, misses or duplicates are involved.

Repo fixtures (test_event_parser.py uses top-level rrweb timestamp 1674291701348 in ms, with seconds only in payload) confirm the top-level event timestamp is ms, while nodestore error timestamps are float seconds, so the merge order is wrong in production.
The analytics record does run before the feature gate, but counting attempted requests is a plausible deliberate choice, so this is a minor design point rather than a defect.

Truthiness checks in validate_timestamp/validate_age do let age:0 with timestamp through and accept neither field, but the impact is limited to malformed input and the requirement of exactly one field is not clearly stated.
normalizeDateTimeParams returns an object, so Boolean(normalizedDateRange) is redundant, but this is a cleanup with no behavioural impact.
get_environment_info does run one recommended-event lookup per issue, but issue lists are small and this is a marginal performance concern without a concrete failure.
Verified in attributes.tsx that the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES check sits inside the filter after the early return when searchQuery is empty, so is_segment, project_id and received show by default.

Flex in layout/flex.tsx only sets align-items and gap when passed, and the old FlexBox set align-items center and gap space(1), so the traceTabsAndVitals replacements change layout, a real but cosmetic regression.
The removed FlexBox set height 100% and the new Flex does not, which is a verified styling change, but its effect depends on parent layout that the finding did not confirm.

The new useQuery drops staleTime, retry and refetchOnWindowFocus and omits environment, and isLoading now tracks isFetching, all verified in the code, but the finding is phrased as a question and the impact is a behaviour change that may be intended.
The story text does contain 'Below is the the most basic example', a correct but trivial docs typo.
The test file no longer posts with application/reports+json, so the BrowserReportsJSONParser path has less coverage, a real but test-gap concern that is capped.

useProjectFromId returns undefined without distinguishing loading from absent, and useProjects exposes initiallyLoaded and fetching, but the finding does not show the replay page rendering before projects load, so the false-error flash is speculative.
The test fixtures do use seconds at top-level timestamp where real recordings use ms, so the tests may hide the unit mismatch, but this is the same root cause as finding 1 and is a test-gap concern.
The class OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans at line 1250 is named for spans while the comment on the Logs class relies on that reading, a naming concern with no functional effect.
